rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative is an initial resumption; opening with the address ‘My servants’ prepares its hearers to accept the message and raises hope of salvation.
rows.anchor: استئناف ابتدائي من خطاب الله لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address initially targets polytheists, as the calls to submit and later references to mockery, denial, arrogance, and disbelief show; this differs from the usual Quranic use of ‘My servants.’
rows.anchor: مراد به المشركون ابتداء بدليل قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report in Sahih al-Bukhari, polytheists who had committed many murders and acts of adultery asked Muhammad whether their deeds could be expiated; verses in al-Furqan and this verse were revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ( أن ناسا من أهل الشرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported occasions of revelation are weak or unknown; taken together, they describe particular instances within the verse’s general address to all polytheists.
rows.anchor: وقد رويت أحاديث عدة في سبب نزول هذه الآية غير حديث البخاري وهي بين ضعيف ومجهول ويستخلص من مجموعها أنها جزئيات لعموم الآية

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq, through Nafi and Ibn Umar, reports that Umar sent the verse to the detained Hisham ibn al-As, who understood it as applying to him and rejoined the Prophet after fleeing to him.
rows.anchor: قال عمر فكتبتها بيدي ثم بعثتها إلى هشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Umar’s statement that God revealed it means he heard it after migrating: the passage was revealed in Mecca, while he was occupied preparing to emigrate and reached Medina before the Prophet.
rows.anchor: يريد أنه سمعه بعد أن هاجر وأنه مما نزل بمكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s description as abundantly forgiving and merciful explains that the sheer number of sins cannot prevent Him from forgiving them all.
rows.anchor: لا يعجزه أن يغفر جميع الذنوب ما بلغ جميعها من الكثرة لأنه شديد الغفران شديد الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse refutes the Murji’ite claim that nothing can harm a person who has faith.
rows.anchor: فبطل بهذه الآية قول المرجئة إنه لا يضر مع الإيمان شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After opening the door of hope, the passage joins its counsel to repent with its ban on despair, using the conjunction and imperative to urge prompt action.
rows.anchor: لما فتح لهم باب الرجاء أعقبه بالإرشاد إلى وسيلة المغفرة معطوفا بالواو وللدلالة على الجمع بين النهي عن القنوط من الرحمة وبين الإنابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inaba means repentance; because both it and repentance carry the sense of returning, their verbs take ‘to’ as their complement. The polytheists are to repent of associating partners by affirming God’s oneness.
rows.anchor: والإنابة : التوبة ولما فيها وفي التوبة من معنى الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to submit means affirming the Prophet and Quran and following the laws of Islam.
rows.anchor: التصديق بالنبي والقرآن واتباع شرائع الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to punishment coming before long, reinforced by the verb ‘comes,’ threatens those who fail to repent and submit.
rows.anchor: إيذان بوعيد قريب إن لم ينيبوا ويسلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite noun denotes punishment generically: it may be worldly punishment, if God wills, or the hereafter’s recompense for disbelief and grave sins; worldly punishment here threatens polytheists specifically.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في العذاب تعريف الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each group has its share in the commands: polytheists must turn to monotheism and Islam, while believers who sin should repent and increase good works; Muslims already possess Islam.
rows.anchor: نصيب المشركين الإنابة إلى التوحيد واتباع دين الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denied aid is help that lets the defeated escape a conqueror’s power against that conqueror; no one can protect anyone from God. Intercession for grave sinners is not this sort of aid, and the warning chiefly addresses polytheists.
rows.anchor: بحيث ينفلت المغلوب من غلبة قاهره كرها على القاهر ولا نصير لأحد على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The best of what was sent down’ is the Quran; this directive is chiefly for polytheists, since Muslims already follow it, as the description of God’s servants shows.
rows.anchor: هو القرآن وهو معنى قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahsan is a superlative meaning complete goodness, not a comparison between parts, since everything in the Quran is good; the construction resembles Joseph preferring prison to what his tempters invited him to.
rows.anchor: اسم تفضيل مستعمل في معنى كامل الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The annexation of ‘best’ to ‘what was sent down’ is an adjective annexed to the noun it describes.
rows.anchor: من إضافة الصفة إلى الموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is the previously mentioned worldly and afterlife punishment, both arriving suddenly without warning; the sword’s punishment reached them at Badr, and the afterlife punishment will come at resurrection.
rows.anchor: والعذاب المذكور في هذه هو العذاب المذكور قبل بنوعيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Lest a soul say’ gives the reason for the commands in verses 54–55, with the purpose lam omitted before an; this omission is common.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأوامر في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A negative la is omitted after an, a common construction illustrated by verses about following the Quran and not following desire.
rows.anchor: وفيه حذف لا } النافية بعد { أن ، وهو شائع أيضا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf commonly supplies the omitted sense as ‘for fear that you do such and such.’
rows.anchor: وعادة صاحب ( الكشاف ) تقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Ashur finds an omitted negative la clearer than al-Kashshaf’s paraphrase, since Arabic uses deletion and addition of la frequently.
rows.anchor: أظهر لكثرة التصرف فيها في كلام العرب بالحذف والزيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul says this so it will not lament its neglect of God’s cause. The words may be an audible cry of regret, adding to hidden regret, or inward speech.
rows.anchor: وظاهر القول إنه القول جهرة وهو شأن الذي ضاق صبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite ‘a soul’ names a category, namely polytheist souls, like the generic soul in the verse about what each soul knows it has brought.
rows.anchor: أن يقول صنف من النفوس وهي نفوس المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labid’s line about death seizing ‘some souls’ uses the plural to mean himself, illustrating a generic or indefinite soul.
rows.anchor: أو يعتلق بعض النفوس حمامها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocative personifies intense regret as a rational being summoned to appear when needed; the formula became a common saying for extreme sorrow.
rows.anchor: بتشبيه الحسرة بالعاقل الذي ينادي ليقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasra is intense remorse, and the alif in the expression substitutes for the speaker’s ya.
rows.anchor: والألف عوض عن ياء المتكلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far alone reads ya hasratai, combining the speaker’s ya with the alif that normally replaces it; his most common reported form has the ya after alif open.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحده { يا حسرتاي } بالجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ‘upon’ with hasra, as is usual, depicts the regret as firmly pressing upon its object.
rows.anchor: بحرف الاستعلاء كما هو غالبها للدلالة على تمكن التحسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ma in ‘for what I neglected’ is a verbal noun, so the phrase means ‘for my neglect.’
rows.anchor: أي على تفريطي في جنب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tafrit means wasting or falling short; the more usual expression is to say farraṭa fīhi.
rows.anchor: يقال : فرطه . والأكثر أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Janb and janib both mean a thing’s side or vicinity; al-sahib bi-l-janb in 4:36 means a neighboring companion.
rows.anchor: والجنب والجانب مترادفان ، وهو ناحية الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes fi complete the verb without a direct object: God’s ‘side’ means His cause, right, attributes, and commands, metaphorically pictured as a master’s neglected preserve; Sabiq al-Barbari’s verse illustrates the wording.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون لتعدية فعل فرطت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase depicts the judged soul as a servant who neglected a master’s sanctuary and livestock; this tableau lets janb retain its literal sense.
rows.anchor: لحال النفس التي أوقفت للحساب والعقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ma is a relative pronoun, farraṭt has a deleted object pronoun referring to it, and the prepositional phrase describes that object: what I neglected in God’s side.
rows.anchor: ويكون المفعول محذوفا وهو الضمير المحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative phrase performs regret for failing to accept the Messenger’s guidance and mocking him; as a circumstantial clause, it admits neglect like a mocker rather than an unaware person.
rows.anchor: خبر مستعمل في إنشاء الندامة على ما فاتها من قبول ما جاءها به الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In is the lightened form of emphatic inna, while the lām in ‘among the mockers’ distinguishes it from negative in.
rows.anchor: مخففة من { إن } المشددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Among the mockers’ more emphatically attributes mockery than ‘a mocker’; Ibn Ashur notes a similar construction in the Quran’s wording about being among the ignorant.
rows.anchor: أشد مبالغة في الدلالة على اتصافهم بالسخرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists would invoke lack of divine guidance to excuse themselves, recycling the argument they had used to silence the Prophet; the old thought remains in their minds at judgment.
rows.anchor: لقصد الاعتذار والتنصل ، تعيد أذهانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘among the God-fearing’ uses the same emphatic construction as ‘among the mockers’ in the previous verse.
rows.anchor: والكلام في من المتقين } مثله في { من الساخرين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wish made upon seeing the punishment is an unqualified wish; law functions as a particle of wishing, and fa-akun is subjunctive as its response.
rows.anchor: وانتصب { فأكون } على جواب التمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Karra means a return, specifically back to earthly life to do good; this wish admits that the speaker formerly did evil.
rows.anchor: وهذا اعتراف بأنها علمت أنها كانت من المسيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statements follow the natural movement of thought at judgment: regret, then excuse, then wish for a return to do good. Reordering them would lose the signal of how these thoughts arise.
rows.anchor: الأصل في الإنشاء ما لم يوجد ما يقتضي العدول عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bala cancels a preceding negative or implied negative to affirm its opposite; here it answers the wish in verse 57, whose law implies that God did not guide the speaker.
rows.anchor: حرف لإبطال منفي أو فيه رائحة النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that God’s signs had come to the sinner elaborates the refutation, like answering an objection by conceding its premise: God did guide the sinner.
rows.anchor: بيان له ، وهو مثل الجواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply pairs the guidance excuse with signs that came and were denied, neglect with the greater offense of arrogance, and the wish to be God-fearing with being a disbeliever; Quranic guidance left no excuse.
rows.anchor: أن الله هداك في الدنيا بالإرشاد بآيات القرآن فقابلت الإرشاد بالتكذيب والاستكبار والكفر بها فلا عذر لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer uses a deliberately scrambled distribution after a summary: it first dispatches the main excuse, then neglect, then the return wish. It skips the mockery claim because that was already an admission.
rows.anchor: وكان الجواب على طريقة النشر المشوش بعد اللف رعيا لمقتضى ذلك التشويش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akbar means greater in magnitude and importance, and creation of the heavens and earth makes plain that the Creator can raise people for judgment.
rows.anchor: أنه أعظم وأهم وأكثر متعلقاتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘People’ here are the people God will recreate as He first created them and return their souls to them.
rows.anchor: الذين يعيد الله خلقتهم كما بدأهم أول مرة ويودع فيهم أرواحهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the greater creation is greater is not offered as new information; it reminds deniers of a known fact they fail to act on.
rows.anchor: والخبر مستعمل في غير معناه لأن كون خلقها أكبر هو أمر معلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proof that resurrection is possible is clear, but those denying it ignore evidence, settle for first impressions, and do not examine counterarguments; they are treated as people without knowledge, leaving ya‘lamun without an object.
rows.anchor: حجة إمكان البعث واضحة ولكن الذين ينكرونها لا يعلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people here are the polytheists who dispute resurrection; the smaller group who knows is the believers. Repeating ‘people’ instead of using a pronoun makes the statement stand independently like a proverb.
rows.anchor: هم الذين يجادلون في آيات البعث وهم المشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The separate wording can circulate as a maxim: those who deny resurrection find it implausible to recreate bodies despite the far greater creation of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: لتكون الجملة مستقلة بالدلالة فتصلح لأن تسير مسير الأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers are likened to the blind and the believers to the seeing; the contrast follows from the preceding distinction between most who do not know and the few who do, and implies misguidance versus guidance.
rows.anchor: ومثل المؤمنين الذين آمنوا به حال البصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating la after the coordinating waw reinforces the denial of equality; the rebuking context suits the added emphasis, and grammarians treat this la as extra.
rows.anchor: النافية بعد واو العطف على النفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although la might have been expected before ‘those who believe,’ the wording emphasizes believers first and makes clear that the sinner is not equal to the righteous person; the two placements give two emphases.
rows.anchor: للتنبيه على أن المقصود عدم مساواة المسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fatir provides a close parallel, with four comparisons alternating between the disbelievers’ side and the believers’ side.
rows.anchor: وقريب منه ما في سورة فاطر في أربع جمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalilan is a circumstantial accusative linked to ‘most people’ in the preceding verse; ma in ‘they remember’ is a verbal noun serving as the grammatical subject.
rows.anchor: و { قليلا } حال من { أكثر الناس } في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase reinforces that most do not know: ‘little’ can imply none, as in the Quran’s ‘little do they believe.’
rows.anchor: لأن قلة التذكر تؤول إلى عدم العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, little can retain its literal sense: disputants begin to reflect but fail to follow the reasoning through, so their incomplete thought has no effect and is like none.
rows.anchor: على صريح معناها ويكون المراد بالقلة عدم التمام

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yatadhakkarun with a third-person ya, matching the apparent discourse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { يتذكرون بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: Asim, Hamza, al-Kisa’i, and Khalaf read tatadhakkarun with a second-person ta, shifting to address the disputants; taking it as an address to all people, with believers as the small reflective group, does not fit the rebuttal’s context.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي وخلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is contextually remote to read the address as all believers and polytheists, with believers accounting for the little reflection; that does not suit the reply or the shift to direct address.
rows.anchor: بعيد عن سياق الرد ولا يلاقي الالتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction before lakin is a verbal embellishment: the sentence could stand separately, but lakin often follows a coordinating waw.
rows.anchor: يكثر أن تقع بعد واو العطف لكانت الجملة جديرة بالفصل دون عطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘most people’ are the polytheists, who greatly outnumbered the believers at the time.
rows.anchor: هم المشركون ، وهم يومئذ أكثر من المؤمنين جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disputes over God’s signs concern both divine oneness and resurrection: the later exchange about partners illustrates the first, while the account of chains and punishment illustrates the second. The creation argument supports resurrection before the call to pray warns against idolatry.
rows.anchor: تشمل مجادلتهم في وحدانية الإلهية كما دل عليه قوله الآتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command returns to the earlier call for exclusive prayer, which followed rebuke of the polytheists and a reminder that only the one who turns to God reflects; after intervening warnings, it embraces believers’ pure worship and connects to the failed prayer of disbelievers.
rows.anchor: عاد الكلام الآن إلى ما يشمل عبادة المؤمنين الخالصة لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prayer earlier meant both worship and asking for a need, this command gathers both senses.
rows.anchor: معنى العبادة ، ومعنى سؤال المطلوب ، أردف بهذا الأمر الجامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Your Lord said’ may refer to God’s inward speech, His will regarding what He would say when willing creation into being.
rows.anchor: ما تعلقت إرادة الله تعلقا صلاحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be literal speech in earlier-revealed verses, such as the command to call on God sincerely; the verse about answering a caller in al-Baqara came later.
rows.anchor: إخبارا عن أقوال مضت في آيات قبل نزول هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that the past tense is figurative for the present: ‘Your Lord says: Call on Me.’
rows.anchor: الماضي مستعملا في الحال مجازا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Al-Nu‘man ibn Bashir reports the Prophet saying ‘supplication is worship,’ then reciting this verse; al-Tirmidhi grades the hadith hasan sahih.
rows.anchor: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du‘a can mean calling, which acknowledges the one called, or requesting; asking God for a need is its common literal meaning.
rows.anchor: بمعنى النداء المستلزم للاعتراف بالمنادى ، ويطلق على الطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Du‘a can also stand figuratively for worship because worship involves calling the one worshipped with reverence and supplication; this usage is less common. Quranic ‘worship’ means singling God out and acknowledging His oneness.
rows.anchor: على عبادة الله على طريق الكناية لأن العبادة لا تخلو من دعاء المعبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istijaba commonly means granting a request; it can also mean accepting worship by forgiving prior shirk and rewarding acts of faith.
rows.anchor: والاستجابة تطلق على إعطاء المسؤول لمن سأله وهو أشهر إطلاقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the command means asking for needs, the response depends on God’s will or fulfillment of the request’s conditions; He may grant the request, something better in this life, or its recompense in the next.
rows.anchor: ترتب الاستجابة على ذلك الطلب معلقا على مشيئة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the command means exclusive worship, God’s response is acceptance of repentance from shirk, which is assured.
rows.anchor: فترتب الاستجابة هو قبول ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairing of the two terms, followed by the reference to worship, signals an ellipsis-like combination: du‘a means both asking and worship, while response means answering and accepting worship’s effects.
rows.anchor: علمنا أن في المعنى المراد ما يشبه الاحتباك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ud‘uni is used for both meanings through the full scope of a shared homonym.
rows.anchor: مستعمل في معنييه بطريقة عموم المشترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astajib is used both literally and figuratively; the context supplies the cue, making the expression concise and comprehensive.
rows.anchor: مستعمل في حقيقته ومجازه ، والقرينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God ‘your Lord’ hints that the addressees owe obedience to His command; this wording does not invoke His favors or describe His attributes.
rows.anchor: في هذا الوصف وإضافته من الإيماء إلى وجوب امتثال أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about hell explains the command by cautioning against refusing God’s call while turning to idols; God does not want His servants led to punishment, and the verse supports asking Him for needs.
rows.anchor: تعليلا يفيد التحذير من إباية دعاء الله حين الإقبال على دعاء الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists prayed to God only when they did not expect their partners to answer, as in the verse about reaching land safely and turning away.
rows.anchor: وكان المشركون لا يضرعون إلى الله إلا إذا لم يتوسموا استجابة شركائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims agree that supplication is legitimate; they disagree with the Mu‘tazilites over whether it can repel a decree. This verse does not settle that dispute because they interpret ‘I will respond’ differently.
rows.anchor: ومشروعية الدعاء لا خلاف فيها بين المسلمين وإنما الخلاف في أنه ينفع في رد القدر أو لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about God being near when His servants call precedes this discussion in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: قريب } الآية في سورة البقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun introduces a clause that hints at the reason for the command.
rows.anchor: وفي الإتيان بالموصول إيماء إلى التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakhirin is a circumstantial accusative from the subject of ‘they will enter’; it means humbled or abased, and the verb dakhira has forms like both mana‘a and fariha.
rows.anchor: و { داخرين } حال من ضمير { سيدخلون }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read sayadkhulun in the active voice, with an open ya and a damma on kha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { سيدخلون } بفتح التحتية

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب
rows.claim: Abu Ja‘far and Ruways from Ya‘qub read yudkhalun in the passive voice, with a damma on ya and a fatha on kha, meaning the angels of punishment will admit them to hell.
rows.anchor: وقرأه أبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب
